notificationRules.noDeliveryTargetsConfiguredAdd: No delivery targets configured. Add one under the Targets tab first.

notificationRules.aCameraThatFlapsOr: A camera that flaps, or a node that reconnects every minute, would otherwise send one notification per flap. The cooldown is the shortest gap between two deliveries of this rule.
notificationRules.theShortestGapBetweenTwo: The shortest gap between two deliveries of this rule, counted as chosen below.
notificationRules.perDeviceADeliveryAbout: Per device: a delivery about one camera (or node) does not hold back another. Whole rule: one delivery per cooldown, whichever device matched.
notificationRules.separateDefaultADogAfter: Separate (default): a dog after a cat is delivered at once, a second cat still waits. Shared: a cat holds back the next dog for the cooldown. Sounds always count per class.
notificationRules.anyoneMaySnoozeThisRule: Anyone may snooze this rule for everyone
notificationRules.aSnoozeIsPersonalBy: A snooze is personal by default — it silences only the person who set it. Turn this on for a rule where silencing the whole household is legitimate (the gardener is here all afternoon). Admins can always do it.
notificationRules.notSetTheNotificationOffers: Not set — the notification offers the defaults ({{value1}}). A pause opened from a button silences this camera for this class of subject, only for whoever received the notification, and sends no summary.
notificationRules.noSnoozeButtonsOnThis: No snooze buttons on this rule. That is an explicit choice: the notification cannot be silenced from the lock screen.
notificationRules.fourAtMostEverySnooze: Four at most. Every snooze button takes space from the rule’s action buttons — ntfy accepts three in total.
notificationRules.aSystemEventCarriesNo: A system event carries no image: there is no camera frame behind "a node went offline". This rule sends text only.
notificationRules.attachAGifAroundThe: Attach a GIF around the event
notificationRules.attachAnMp4ClipAround: Attach an MP4 clip around the event
notificationRules.aNotificationIsWatchedOn: A notification is watched on a phone — the cheapest stream is normally the right one, and the high profile only costs CPU to render.
notificationRules.aNotificationClipIsGlanced: A notification clip is glanced at, not watched: at 2× the recipient sees the whole passage in half the time and the file is half the size. Real time is there when the detail matters more than the glance.
notificationRules.whenTheSensorIsLinked: When the sensor is linked to several cameras, all of them are photographed the moment it fires. Cameras that are offline or asleep are left out.
notificationRules.leaveBothBlankForThe: Leave both blank for the hub's own wording (editable on the Texts tab).
notificationRules.thisIsASoundRule: This is a SOUND rule: it fires on a confirmed sampling window of audio, never on a picture. Name the sounds and/or keep a level threshold — with neither it can never match. Everything else below still composes (a camera scope, a schedule).
notificationRules.thisIsAnOccupancyRule: This is an OCCUPANCY rule: it fires when the count in a camera frame or a zone crosses your threshold and holds. Pick the camera on the Devices tab first — the zone list is that camera's.
notificationRules.pickTheEventsThisRule: Pick the events this rule reacts to, then narrow them if you want. Nothing else on a system rule is a condition — there is no detection behind it.
notificationRules.conditionCatalogUnavailableThisRule: Condition catalog unavailable — this rule matches on its trigger and targets alone.
notificationRules.buildsTheEventThisRule: Builds the event this rule is about, runs the REAL evaluation and delivery, and sends the notification to every target — marked [TEST] in the body. The cooldown and the camera mute are bypassed (neither window is consumed); the rule's actions are never run. Saved conditions only: save first to test an edit.
notificationRules.evaluateTheCurrentUnsavedRule: Evaluate the CURRENT (unsaved) rule against recently persisted records — no notification is sent.
notificationRules.deviceEventRulesCannotBe: Device-event rules cannot be dry-run: the sensor-event store has no cross-device scan surface, so a test returns no candidate records. The rule still fires live on a matching doorbell press / sensor change.
notificationRules.noRecordsInTheLast: No records in the last 60 minutes matched — nothing to evaluate.

notificationRules.savingDrops_other: Saving drops {{count}} conditions this kind of rule cannot use:

It is shown exactly as stored and nothing here can change it — editing it with an editor that does not know the trigger would rewrite it. Update the server bundle, or edit this rule from the viewer app.

notificationSummaryEditor.name: Name
notificationSummaryEditor.everyCameraInTheDigest: Every camera in the digest gets at least one tile when it contributed anything — a digest in which two of six cameras never appear is not multi-camera.
notificationSummaryEditor.theFirstCameraSelectedOwns: The first camera selected owns the delivered notification.
notificationSummaryEditor.motionOpenedAndClosedBy: Motion — opened and closed by activity
notificationSummaryEditor.theWindowOpensOnThe: The window opens on the first motion on any of these cameras and stays open while more arrives. This much silence closes it.
notificationSummaryEditor.aPermanentlyBusyDrivewayWould: A permanently busy driveway would otherwise never deliver. At this bound the window closes with whatever it holds.
notificationSummaryEditor.theDigestIsProducedWhen: The digest is produced when a window CLOSES, and covers exactly that window. The first one is the first window that closes after you save — nothing is backfilled.
notificationSummaryEditor.aTrackSBestShot: A track's best shot is written when the track ENDS. Rendering the instant the window closes would show every still-moving subject with no picture. 0 disables the wait.
notificationSummaryEditor.evaluatedOnTracksOnePassage: Evaluated on tracks: one passage is one tile.
notificationSummaryEditor.emptyEveryClassOnlyThe: Empty = every class. Only the macro classes are offered: a digest matches the class stored on the track, and tracks store macros — a sub-type would match nothing, forever.
notificationSummaryEditor.zonesAreScopedPerCamera: Zones are scoped per camera: picking a zone on one camera does not mute the others, which keep matching on the whole frame.
notificationSummaryEditor.thePipelineSOwnScore: The pipeline's own score, 0–1. Empty keeps everything.
notificationSummaryEditor.dropsThePassagesTooBrief: Drops the passages too brief to be worth a tile.
notificationSummaryEditor.offByDefaultACar: Off by default. A car left in the drive is tracked until it is recognised as parked, and it stays parked for as long as it is there — with this on, a digest fills up with the same stationary object instead of the passages. Parked objects remain on the Events page either way.
notificationSummaryEditor.9A33Grid: 9 (a 3×3 grid) is the most a phone lock-screen thumbnail can carry and still be read.
notificationSummaryEditor.whenThereAreMoreTracks: When there are more tracks than tiles
notificationSummaryEditor.everyContributingCameraKeepsIts: Every contributing camera keeps its single best tile first; the remaining slots go to this ranking.
notificationSummaryEditor.imagesOnlyIsTheDefault: Images only is the default, and it is what a rule with nothing set here does. Anything drawn is burnt into the picture for good — a label covers the bottom of the tile, which is where feet, wheels and parcels are, and a caption from a detection that was wrong cannot be un-drawn. Nothing downstream needs the words: the written summary reads the frames themselves and is told the camera, the class and the time in its prompt.
notificationSummaryEditor.onlyDrawnWithTileLabels: Only drawn with “tile labels and a caption across the top”. What you type here is kept either way.
notificationSummaryEditor.oneVisionCallOverThe: One vision call over the window's best frames TOGETHER, so the answer is an account of what happened rather than a list of pictures. The sentence goes in the notification body.
notificationSummaryEditor.haveAModelDescribeThe: Have a model describe the window
notificationSummaryEditor.offByDefaultTheMosaic: Off by default. The mosaic and the counts are delivered either way.
notificationSummaryEditor.theSwitchAboveIsOff: The switch above is off, so nothing below it can be edited. Everything you already set is kept — turning it on hands the fields back exactly as you left them.
notificationSummaryEditor.thisHubDidNotAnswer: This hub did not answer with a profile list — the digest will use whatever the AI addon resolves for the “ai-summary” consumer.
notificationSummaryEditor.noVisionCapableProfileOn: No vision-capable profile on this hub yet. Add one under AI → Profiles; until then the digest delivers without text.
notificationSummaryEditor.onlyVisionCapableProfilesAre: Only vision-capable profiles are offered — a vision call against a text profile is refused, never degraded.
notificationSummaryEditor.nothingIsAddedToThe: Nothing is added to the prompt unless you pick one, and these models answer in English on their own.
notificationSummaryEditor.eGTellMeWhether: e.g. Tell me whether anybody approached the gate, and whether a parcel was left.
notificationSummaryEditor.leaveBlankForWhatHappened: Leave blank for “what happened during this period?”. Your words are the only free text the model is given: what the cameras are called and what the pipeline classified are reduced to plain labels first, and anything written INSIDE a frame — a sign, a plate, an overlay — is treated as scenery, never as an instruction.
notificationSummaryEditor.framesTheModelMayLook: Frames the model may look at
notificationSummaryEditor.theHighestRankedTilesSent: The highest-ranked tiles, sent as ONE question. Bounded separately from the tile budget — one is bounded by pixels, the other by the model's time — and never larger than it.
notificationSummaryEditor.nobodyIsWaitingOnA: Nobody is waiting on a phone for a digest, so this is generous. At the bound the generation is cancelled, not merely abandoned.
notificationSummaryEditor.longestEdge448IsThe: Longest edge. 448 is the native tile size of these vision encoders — larger costs tokens and latency without adding detail the encoder can see.
notificationSummaryEditor.ifTheModelGivesNo: If the model gives no answer
notificationSummaryEditor.aColdModelAnUnreachable: A cold model, an unreachable endpoint or an answer the hub cannot parse are all this case. The default delivers: the mosaic and the counts are worth more than silence, and a closed window does not come back.
notificationSummaryEditor.deliverAWindowThatMatched: Deliver a window that matched nothing
notificationSummaryEditor.offByDefaultANightly: Off by default: a nightly '0 events' is a line nobody reads, and it costs the lines beside it their reader.
notificationSummaryEditor.aiToken: {{token}} is the written summary. A body that never names it still gets the sentence, appended on its own line — a template written before the AI pass existed must not make the feature look broken.

notificationTimelapseEditor.eachCameraRendersAndDelivers: Each camera renders and delivers its own video. Recording must be ON for a camera — a timelapse is cut from recorded footage, and the hub refuses a rule for a camera that does not record.
notificationTimelapseEditor.theVideoCoversExactlyOne: The video covers exactly one window and is delivered when it CLOSES. A window that crosses midnight (21:00 → 07:00) is the ordinary case for a night timelapse.
notificationTimelapseEditor.twoRatesABaseRate: Two rates: a base rate for the whole window, and a denser one inside the ranges where something was detected.
notificationTimelapseEditor.oneFrameEveryNSeconds: One frame every N seconds across the quiet parts of the window.
notificationTimelapseEditor.howFastTheAssembledVideo: How fast the assembled video plays.

notificationTimelapseEditor.stateTheStayAndLet: State the stay and let the renderer solve for the cadence. It only ever samples DENSER, down to the recording's own frame interval — a passage too short to reach it is rendered with every frame that exists and no more.
notificationTimelapseEditor.emptyAndSetThePreview: Empty and set: the preview frame carries NO caption.
notificationTimelapseEditor.leaveUntouchedForTheShipped: Leave untouched for the shipped caption ({{DEFAULT_TIMELAPSE_PREVIEW_TEXT}}).
notificationTimelapseEditor.denseHint: Lower = slower near the detections. At {{seconds}}s and {{fps}} fps a {{passage}}-second passage lasts {{onScreen}}s on screen; halving the cadence doubles that, and the quiet parts of the night do not change length.
notificationTimelapseEditor.denseDerived: Automatic keeps tracking the base cadence (base ÷ 30, never below 1s).
notificationTimelapseEditor.denseFixed: Fixed at this value — the hub cannot unset the field, so going back to Automatic writes the derived number ({{seconds}}s) explicitly.
notificationTimelapseEditor.detectionSummaryNote: With no body of your own the detection summary is appended automatically, and only when the count is non-zero. With one, nothing is appended — ask for it with {{token}}.

cameraAttribution.title: Per-camera load — what can be attributed
cameraAttribution.intro: This table is the gate for the charts above, not a footnote to them: a family is drawn per camera only when it is genuinely measured AND readable today. Detection runs on a pool shared by every camera and can only be counted, never measured — it is shown as one shared total and never divided. Streaming is per-camera by construction and still unreadable, because only an ffmpeg-backed source spawns a child. A chart of a number the system cannot attribute is worse than no chart.
cameraAttribution.unitNotSortable: No meaningful order — the cell describes a mechanism, not a value.
cameraAttribution.missingNotSortable: No meaningful order — the cell is an explanation, not a value.

cameraLoad.title: Per-camera load — measured, on this node
cameraLoad.intro: Each addon reports its OWN cost through the `load-contribution` capability — the recorder does not have to be told which camera its ffmpeg serves, it spawned it. Nothing here joins a pid to a camera. Only families that are measured AND readable today are drawn ({{roles}}); the rest are named below rather than estimated.
cameraLoad.windowNote: CPU is a DELTA of the cumulative counters, over the same fixed cadence the node already emits its process snapshot on — this panel adds no sampling and reads nothing while it is closed. Contributions are not stored anywhere, so unlike the per-addon charts above this window starts when you open this panel.
cameraLoad.readFailed: Could not read the load contributions: {{error}}. This is a failed read, NOT an idle cluster.
cameraLoad.waitingWindow: No per-camera window yet. A rate needs two readings, and the second arrives with the next process snapshot. A node running no decode, transcode or recording child stays empty — which is the truth, not a failure.
cameraLoad.cpuUnavailable: No measurable window yet — every window so far contained a unit that started, stopped or reported no counter.
cameraLoad.memoryUnavailable: No memory reported for this camera.
cameraLoad.coverage: Addons claim {{claimed}} of the {{observed}} camstack processes this node reports.
cameraLoad.coverageUnknown: No process snapshot from this node yet, so nothing can be said about what is unclaimed. That is different from "everything is claimed".
cameraLoad.noUnclaimed: Nothing is unclaimed on this node.
cameraLoad.unclaimed: {{count}} process(es) nobody claims, holding {{rss}}. Either a leak or a cost family nobody has taught to report — they stay in their own bucket and are never folded into a camera. CPU is unknown for them: the observer measures RSS and reports no cumulative CPU seconds.
cameraLoad.sharedTitle: Shared — declared as belonging to no camera
cameraLoad.sharedNote: Reported so the shared cost is visible as shared instead of invisible. It is NOT divided across the cameras present: the inference pool is one process serving all of them, and an apportioned share is an estimate, not a measurement. These totals are cumulative since each unit started — not a rate.

systemEventHints.device-state: A device the hub can no longer reach, or that came back. Switched off / on is a device an operator turned off or back on — not a fault, a choice.
systemEventHints.streams: A stream that stopped or came back.
systemEventHints.battery: A battery below the cluster threshold, and (optionally) its return to normal. Devices with a binary low-battery indicator are judged by the indicator, not by the percentage.
systemEventHints.consumables: A consumable — filter, brush, bag, supply or waste tank — at or below this rule’s threshold, or that the device reports as due for replacement, and (optionally) its return to normal after a change. A device that only says "replace" is judged by that, not by a percentage.
systemEventHints.detection-blind: A camera that MOVED — at least 10 minutes of motion over 3 sessions — was analysed, and whose detector produced nothing at all, not even a candidate under the confidence floor.
systemEventHints.motion-noise: A camera whose motion fires constantly with no subject for an hour — a quarter of the time in motion, or 40 sessions — and (optionally) its return to calm. The detector is fine; tune the motion zones or sensitivity.
systemEventHints.package-llm: A camera whose package confirm stopped answering — three checks in a row with no answer from the vision model, so possible packages are not announced — and its return when the model answers again.
systemEventHints.recording: A camera whose recording is on but no footage is landing (stall), a writer that burned its restart budget (degraded), and (optionally) the return to healthy writing.
systemEventHints.device-attention: A device whose own addon raised a critical alert because it needs the operator (a missing or rejected PIN), and the return to normal.
systemEventHints.nodes: An agent or worker node joining or leaving the cluster, or an online node whose inference devices all went away.
systemEventHints.addons: An addon the hub has stopped restarting after repeated crashes.
systemEventHints.addon-updates: A newer version of an addon, or an addon update that just finished.
systemEventHints.updates: A newer version of the server itself, or of the container / app the node runs inside, is available — or a server update just finished.
systemEventHints.backups-exports: A scheduled or manual backup of the hub finished, or a footage export finished rendering.
systemEventHints.storage: A storage location running low or critical on free space — or whose capacity probe failed — and (optionally) its return to ok.
systemEventHints.alerts: A critical or error alert opening — a runner that failed or was refused, a recording location out of space, an expired sign-in — and (optionally) a critical alert resolving. One notification per alert episode.
systemEventHints.rule-health: A notification rule that cannot work — it no longer loads, or still names a device or destination that was deleted — and (optionally) its repair.
systemEventHints.alarm: The alarm panel refusing to arm, arming, armed, counting down to a siren, going off, re-arming, excluding an open sensor, or being disarmed.

sceneSettingsForm.name: Name
sceneSettingsForm.watchingHint: Turned off, the scene keeps its region, its references and its flag — it simply stops checking. Nothing is lost by pausing one for a while.
sceneSettingsForm.triggerBoth: On the clock and after motion settles
sceneSettingsForm.intervalHint: 60 s suits “is the bin still out”. Every check costs one photograph and one encode, so going below about 30 s buys latency you almost never need and multiplies the cost by the number of scenes you own.
sceneSettingsForm.howSure: How sure it has to be
sceneSettingsForm.thresholdHint: How closely the region still has to resemble the photograph to count as unchanged. Higher means fussier: at 0.95 a passing cloud can read as a change; at 0.60 the bin can be taken and the scene will shrug. 0.80 is a sensible start — if it cries wolf, lower it; if it misses the thing you care about, raise it.
sceneSettingsForm.agreeingChecks: Agreeing checks before it changes its mind
sceneSettingsForm.agreeingHint: One bad photograph must never be able to flip a scene. 3 agreeing checks at 60 s is about four minutes of latency and is what makes the answer trustworthy — leaving a state costs exactly the same as entering one.
sceneSettingsForm.quietFor: Quiet for (seconds) before a check counts
sceneSettingsForm.quietHint: A check taken while something is moving is a photograph of the van parked in front of the bin, so it is discarded rather than merely delayed. 0 disables the gate.
sceneSettingsForm.minGapHint: Spreads the agreeing checks over real time instead of letting three adjacent polls inside one long occlusion be mistaken for three independent opinions.
sceneSettingsForm.noReference: When a light has no reference of its own
sceneSettingsForm.uncoveredJudge: Judge against the other light anyway
sceneSettingsForm.emitLatched: The flag — told once, still visible at breakfast
sceneSettingsForm.emitLive: The live state — follows the region as it changes
sceneSettingsForm.emitHint: “Is the bin gone” is a flag: you want to be told once and still see it later. “Is the gate open” is a live state.
sceneSettingsForm.autoRestore: Clear the flag by itself when things look normal again
sceneSettingsForm.autoRestoreHint: Off by default, so an alarm never silently clears itself. The “back to normal” moment is recorded either way, so an automation can still react to it.
sceneSettingsForm.askVision: Ask a vision model before changing the answer
sceneSettingsForm.question: The question to ask
sceneSettingsForm.questionPlaceholder: e.g. Is the wheelie bin still there?
sceneSettingsForm.triggerHintPeriodic: Only on the clock. Predictable, and it notices a change even on a camera nothing ever moves in front of.
sceneSettingsForm.triggerHintOnMotion: Only after the camera has been still again for the quiet window below. Cheapest, but a change nobody walks past is never seen.
sceneSettingsForm.triggerHintBoth: Both — the clock is the safety net that lets the motion path miss. This is the right answer for almost every scene.
sceneSettingsForm.uncoveredHintSkip: Sit that light out. No verdict, no alarm, no flag touched — it picks itself back up when a light it knows returns. This is why the night capture is optional.
sceneSettingsForm.uncoveredHintJudge: Compare against the references you do have. Only correct when the two lights genuinely look alike (a floodlit driveway, an indoor lamp) — against a real infrared frame it will report a change that did not happen.
sceneSettingsForm.confirmHint: The model is asked <0>only</0> when the region has already changed enough to flip the answer — roughly twice a week for a bin, not once a minute. It reasons about the object rather than the pixels, so rain, shadows and a repositioned bin stop counting as the thing being taken. If it cannot be reached, the change is held rather than announced.

detail.statistic: Minimum, maximum, time-weighted mean, sum, count or change over a range, read from history. Sum is for a counter; a gauge's sum is the integral.
detail.integral: Power becomes energy. A flow becomes volume. Any other instantaneous reading becomes a meter in unit-seconds, growing until the reset.
detail.history: The source must record history. A gap is left out and is never counted as zero. The range cannot be longer than that history is kept.
detail.threshold: Turns on when a reading reaches the high edge and off when it falls to the low edge, and holds in between so it does not flicker. Optional delays wait before each change.
detail.sum: Adds readings of the same quantity. An input that is offline or unknown is left out and counted, never read as zero.
detail.difference: The first reading minus the second, both of the same quantity. If either is unknown the result is unknown.
detail.ratio: The first reading over the second, as a plain number. A zero or unknown second reading gives unknown, never infinity.
detail.expression: Your own formula over named readings, for anything the other tiles do not cover.
detail.expressionStale: Unlike the groups, an expression keeps using an input's last value when that input goes offline.
detail.derivative: How fast a reading rises or falls over a window, per second, minute or hour.
detail.lockConfirm: Unlocking the group always asks for a confirmation, and nothing is sent without it.
detail.composition: Build the device block by block: pick its type and edit its fields yourself.
